name: Rictus Entertainment
sovereign_territory: The Rictus Pleasure Corridor — a 14-kilometer strip of sovereign entertainment territory carved through the former downtown core of Detroit, plus six 'Rictus Enclaves' embedded within other city-states across the corridor (negotiated sovereign entertainment zones within host cities). Headquarters: The Grinhouse, a 112-story entertainment megastructure in the heart of the Detroit Corridor.
founding_story: Rictus was founded in 2138 by Casimir Voll, a former theme park architect and neural interface developer who had grown disgusted with what he called 'the flatness of passive media.' Voll's thesis was simple and, critics argued, deeply dangerous: human beings would pay any price for experiences that felt more real than reality. He launched Rictus with a single product — the DeepDream Suite, a full-sensory neural immersion pod that delivered experiences indistinguishable from lived memory. The first Rictus parlor opened in a repurposed Detroit theater in 2138. By 2142, there were 400 locations across the corridor. By 2147, Rictus had declared sovereign territory in Detroit, arguing that its 'experience economy' constituted a new form of civic infrastructure. They weren't entirely wrong. The Detroit Pleasure Corridor now draws more visitors annually than any other single destination in GLMZ. Voll died in 2155 under circumstances the corponation describes as 'a voluntary full-immersion retirement' — widely understood to mean he jacked into a DeepDream Suite and never came back out. The company has been run by a rotating executive council since.
security_force: The Smilers — 11,000 security personnel famous for their unsettling customer-service demeanor. Smilers are trained to de-escalate with extreme psychological precision and escalate with equal precision when required. They wear white uniforms with reflective face shields that produce a slight upward curve at the corners — hence the name. The Smilers also operate a covert intelligence division called the Curtain, which monitors for corporate espionage, talent poaching, and what Rictus terms 'experience piracy' (illegal duplication of proprietary neural content).
key_detail: Rictus's DeepDream technology is both its greatest asset and its most controversial product. Extended use causes a well-documented neurological condition called Drift — a progressive inability to distinguish immersive memory from lived experience. Rictus acknowledges Drift in its user agreements (buried in clause 47-F) but has successfully lobbied against mandatory health warnings in seven of the nine major city-states. The corponation also operates a quiet secondary business: harvesting anonymized emotional and experiential data from DeepDream sessions, which it sells to advertisers, political consultants, and — according to several investigative journalists who have since gone quiet — at least two intelligence agencies.
relationship_to_big_20: Big 20 member, ranked approximately 8th by revenue. Rictus is simultaneously beloved and feared by other Big 20 members — beloved because its entertainment infrastructure drives consumer spending across all sectors, feared because its data harvesting capabilities give it leverage over virtually everyone. At least three other Big 20 corponations are known to have purchased Rictus experiential data on their own executives.
full_text: RICTUS ENTERTAINMENT & IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCE CORPONATION — The dominant force in neural recreation and immersive entertainment across GLMZ, Rictus operates from its 112-story Grinhouse headquarters in the sovereign Detroit Pleasure Corridor, a 14-kilometer strip of entertainment sovereignty that the corponation carved from the former Detroit downtown core. Founded in 2138 by the visionary and ultimately self-consumed Casimir Voll, Rictus built its empire on a single insight: people will pay everything for experiences that feel realer than real. The DeepDream Suite — a full-sensory neural immersion system capable of manufacturing memories indistinguishable from lived experience — is Rictus's flagship product and the source of both its staggering ₩203 billion annual revenue and its most enduring controversy. Drift, the neurological degradation caused by extended DeepDream use, affects an estimated 2.3 million users across the corridor, but Rictus has successfully suppressed mandatory health warnings in most jurisdictions. The Smilers, Rictus's 11,000-strong security force, maintain the Pleasure Corridor's paradoxically cheerful order, while the covert Curtain division protects proprietary neural content and harvests user data for sale to advertisers, political operatives, and unnamed intelligence buyers. A Big 20 member ranked roughly 8th by revenue, Rictus is simultaneously indispensable to the corridor economy and deeply feared — its data repositories contain the emotional and experiential memories of millions, and the corponation has never been shy about monetizing them. Voll himself is believed to be permanently immersed somewhere in the Grinhouse's private server farm, dreaming whatever comes after a life spent manufacturing dreams for others.
